_note: WHICH MAP, WAVE TABLE AND PLATE BELONG TO WHICH LEVEL. GameScene reads this: it takes a level id and loads that level's map, waves and plate through here, which is what made a second and third level possible at all. The note this replaces still claimed GameScene loaded waves.json directly and was single-level on purpose; that stopped being true when the level-aware refactor landed, and a file describing an architecture the repository no longer has is worse than no note.
_lane: laneLengthPx is the walked length of the painted road, summed over the level's waypoints, rounded to 0.1. BOTH are now measured from the level's own map file by that one method: level 1 from map.json, level 2 from map_level2.json. Level 2 previously carried 1916.7, a figure that arrived with the plate before the lane was traced and was never checked; the traced waypoints walk 1955.3, so it was short by 38.6 px. It is recorded because wave spacing is only comparable between levels that walk the same distance, and the two here differ by 1.1%, which is not enough to retune. Re-measure after any retrace rather than carrying a number forward. LEVEL 3 IS THE SHORT ONE: 1560.2 px, both routes, against 1976.9 and 1955.3. That is 21% less road than level 1, which is far outside the 1.1% that made levels 1 and 2 comparable, so its wave spacing is NOT copied from theirs and its health total is not directly comparable either. Its two branches walk 1560.18 and 1560.15 -- equal to 0.03 px, which is in the geometry rather than arranged, and means neither gate is the fast one.
_roadmap: WHERE A LEVEL SITS ON THE WORLD MAP: nowhere in this file, because it is the level's PLACE IN THIS LIST. mapPosition used to be here, one hand-authored pair per level, and it is why the trail on that screen was wrong -- level 4 sat at x 0.03 because the old full-size cards could not be stacked and there was nowhere else to put it, so the path drawn in level order ran the width of the screen backwards and read as though it skipped level 1 altogether. Its own note admitted the corner it had been painted into. A road cannot have positions that disagree with its order, so it no longer has positions: WorldMapScene lays every node out along one curve by index and the levels here take the first slots on it. Moving a level means moving its row. Adding one means a row here and a card in art.json's worldMap.cards -- a test fails the build without both.
_plannedLevels: HOW LONG THE ROAD IS, the unbuilt stretch included. Every slot past the last row above draws darkened and padlocked, so the map shows how far the campaign is meant to run instead of stopping at whatever shipped last. Raising it costs nothing and adds road; a value below the number of levels above is ignored, since a level that exists always gets a slot.
_towers: WHICH TOWERS A LEVEL CAN DRAW, beyond draft.json's shared pool. draft.json's towerWeights is every level's pool; extraTowerWeights adds to it for one level and is absent everywhere else. The Ima Dummy Tower is level 1's only for now, which is what the brief asked for and also what keeps levels 2 and 3 comparable to the numbers they were tuned against.
_unlockedBy:
WHICH LEVEL OPENS THIS ONE, by id, or null for the one that is open from the start. It replaces `runsClearedToUnlock`, a COUNT of cleared runs, and the swap fixes three things a count could not.
FIRST, A COUNT CANNOT SAY WHICH LEVELS. The save recorded how many runs had been cleared and not which ones, so clearing level 1 three times opened level 4 -- and START RUN asks for the furthest unlocked level, so it would hand that player level 4 having never seen 2 or 3. Both of the notes this replaces spent a paragraph each explaining that the brief's requested value had to be raised to stop exactly that, and admitted the gate still could not be made specific. A prerequisite id is specific by construction.
SECOND, THE CAPTIONS WERE ABOUT THE WRONG THING. A locked node read `Clear 2 runs to unlock`, which is true of the arithmetic and useless to a player: two runs of WHAT? It names the level now.
THIRD, IT NEEDS THE SAVE TO KNOW WHAT WAS BEATEN, which is the `clearedLevels` field and the migration in Save.ts -- the new save field the old note said fixing this properly would need. `isLevelCleared` is a lookup now rather than a derivation, so it cannot be wrong.
A level naming a prerequisite that does not exist is unreachable rather than open, and a test fails on it, because an unreachable level is a typo and an accidentally open one is a skipped level.
_nextLevel: THERE IS NO `next` FIELD AND THERE MUST NOT BE. The level after this one is the level that names it as a prerequisite, which is the same fact read the other way round -- a second field would be a second opinion, and the two would eventually disagree about which level follows which. `Levels.nextLevelId` does the lookup. It returns null past the last built level, which is what the victory screen needs in order to offer LEVEL SELECT instead of pointing NEXT LEVEL at a COMING SOON slot.
